name: trainline_machine_learning_engineer
gaps_acknowledged: No experience productionising ML models or owning deployment and maintenance at scale
No Terraform, MLflow or MLOps platform experience
No CI/CD ownership or stated agile delivery experience
No recommendation systems or optimisation algorithms experience
No transport industry or GIS experience
No LLM agent-building experience (has LLM evaluation, fine-tuning and RAG)
key_tailoring_decisions: Led the CV with TikTok Shop UK consumer marketplace analytics as the closest honest analogue to Trainline's consumer-product ML, and reframed the KPI bullet around whether an initiative moved its target metric

Made experimentation and evaluation rigour the spine of the letter (A/B testing, offline and online evaluation, calibration over headline AUC, causal forests with null results reported) rather than claiming MLOps depth

Renamed the skills lines to the posting's own headings (Machine Learning, Statistical Methodologies, data extraction / data manipulation / feature engineering) and surfaced the nice-to-haves she genuinely has: LLM fine-tuning, RAG and knowledge graphs

Named the production gap explicitly in the letter (no model owned in production, no Spark, Terraform or MLflow) instead of hiding it, and removed a 'CI-aware workflows' skills phrase that her profile does not support
Used one independently verified Trainline fact (over 270 rail and coach carriers, from thetrainline.com/about-us) as the 'why this company' hook
warnings: MANDATORY REVIEWER SUBAGENT NOT RUN: the Agent tool refused with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached (20)' because all 20 sibling application agents were running. Per the brief's do-not-retry instruction I did not retry. I performed the grounding audit, AI-tells audit, requirement-coverage check and independent company verification myself instead. This application has had no second-pair-of-eyes review.

This posting is pitched at an experienced production ML engineer, not a graduate. It asks for experience productionising ML models, Spark, Docker and Terraform, MLflow, and CI/CD, and expects ownership of the full lifecycle through deployment and maintenance. She has none of the production or big-data stack. She is credible on the modelling, statistics and evaluation half of the job and on the consumer-marketplace domain, but a hiring manager screening on 'has shipped a model to production' will filter her out. Worth submitting as a stretch given Trainline's stated learning-and-development emphasis, but expect a low response rate.
The posting says nothing about visa sponsorship. The letter states her position plainly (right to work now, Skilled Worker sponsorship needed in about two years) so it is not a hidden surprise.
Hybrid requirement is a minimum 60% office attendance over a 12-week period in London. She is London based, so this passes, but it is firmer than most postings.
